A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InterActHuman. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across the revision, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation benchmarks, user-study outcomes, and conditioning ablations in Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds talking-head benchmarks, runtime measurements, mask analyses, a cache ablation, and evaluations with four to five people.

M1.justification: The reference-image injection, mask predictor, cached-mask audio conditioning, training objectives, and inference procedure remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1. Appendix C newly documents implementation choices and long-video generation without establishing a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original evaluation coverage and adds single-person talking-head evaluations on CelebV-HQ and RAVDESS, explicit low/high-motion scenarios, and four-to-five-person generation tests (Tables 6–7 and 9–13). These substantially broaden the evaluated populations and operating conditions.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds MultiTalk to the existing multi-person comparison. New Tables 6–7 evaluate SadTalker, Hallo, VExpress, EchoMimic, Hallo-3, and Loopy alongside OmniHuman. HunyuanVideo-Avatar appears only in the capability matrix, rather than a reported generation benchmark.

E3.justification: The original protocols are retained, while new experiments introduce FID for talking-head evaluation, mask IoU across selected denoising steps and layers under two motion regimes, and cached-versus-uncached testing. Runtime is measured per forward pass at 720p and 109 frames on one A100 while varying reference count (Section 4.2 and Appendix A).

E4.justification: Beyond the unchanged global-audio, ID-embedding, and fixed-mask ablation, v2 tests mask refinement across steps and layers, sensitivity to motion, cache necessity, scaling beyond three people, and computational overhead. Figure 5 adds an overlapping-subject mask-failure case. These directly investigate previously untested aspects of the central mechanism.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new keypoint-motion variances in Table 11 describe motion regimes, rather than uncertainty in model performance.

E6.justification: Existing result entries in Tables 1–4 remain numerically unchanged. v2 adds MultiTalk results, including Sync-D 7.671 and FVD 35.472, and substantial new benchmark, runtime, mask-IoU, and scaling results. Table 12 reports Sync-D 6.921 with caching versus 11.046 without caching; these are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1's model.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 adds a short analytical cost-scaling argument: increasing latent count from 28 to 28+n yields relative self-attention cost (1+n/28)^2. The existing flow-matching formulation, mask equations, and algorithmic mathematics are unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the broad description of controllable multi-concept videos with the more specific capability of two-to-three-person dialogue generation or customization from multiple reference images. The main contributions and conclusion otherwise retain the same claims about layout-aligned conditioning and generation quality.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations linking cache removal to identity-assignment degradation and larger-person-count scalability to independent mask prediction. It also identifies overlapping subjects and coarse VAE resolution as sources of mask failure. Appendix A.4 somewhat overstates combined-mask superiority: layer 20 has higher final-step IoU in both Tables 9 and 10.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies sliding-window continuation, the SAM2 confidence threshold of 0.5, focal-loss parameters, and the audio attention window. v2 also documents model overhead and reports providing a Wan2.1 reimplementation and data-processing code. Data provenance changes from an unspecified internal source to OpenHumanVid plus self-collected videos, without establishing that the underlying training corpus was replaced.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ingredients, OpenHumanVid, HunyuanVideo-Avatar, and MultiTalk references. Section 2 distinguishes Ingredients' layout prediction from audio-conditioned generation, while Appendix A.3 and Table 8 position InterActHuman against concurrent multi-person systems. The broader literature review and positioning remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: v2 polishes introduction and method prose, folds reference-image injection into the preliminaries, and reorganizes the appendices around a new experimental-results section. It also updates authorship and conference front matter and adds disclosure statements. The overall narrative and most existing passages remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5–13 and a new mask-failure Figure 5, substantially expanding the experimental displays. The original Figure 5 is retained as Figure 6, Table 1 gains a comparator row, and the document adopts conference formatting with revised table sizing and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central cached-mask mechanism through direct mask-IoU measurements, a cache ablation, motion and population-scaling tests, and an explicit failure analysis. These address important gaps left by v1's alternative-conditioning comparisons, while added implementation details improve reproducibility. Missing uncertainty estimates and some overstated mask-refinement interpretations remain limitations, but do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and transparency.
